findings: The primary specimen is a convincing Northern Waterthrush: long-bodied warbler proportions, relatively short narrow tail, fine pointed bill, long dusky-pink legs, plain brownish upperparts, narrow pale supercilium, and dense dark streaking through the throat and underparts agree with the reference photographs and direct sources.

The plate contains exactly one primary specimen with one head, one bill, one tail, two convincingly attached legs, and intact feet. The near-side wing is complete; the far-side wing is naturally occluded by the side-on pose with no malformed or duplicated structure visible.

The detached wing and head are clearly separated supplementary studies rather than extra birds or structures attached to the primary specimen. Both are anatomically coherent, and the bills in the primary and head study have consistent, plausible proportions.
All visible identification, habitat, behavior, taxonomy, and measurement text is legible and matches the proposed profile without duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical wording.

The Cornell measurement set is reproduced faithfully with its Both Sexes qualifier: length 4.7–5.5 in (12–14 cm), weight 0.5–0.7 oz (14.7–19.2 g), and wingspan 8.9–10.0 in (22.5–25.5 cm). Audubon's different supported measurement set does not create a profile conflict.

The body-length schematic now labels 4.7 in (12 cm) at the bottom and 5.5 in (14 cm) at the top, increases upward, agrees with the printed length range, and retains the SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE notice. Its unlabeled interior ticks are noncontradictory subdivisions.

The warm brown rendering remains compatible with the brownish to olive-brown variation visible in the references and sources; the narrow buff-to-whitish eyebrow and heavily streaked pale underparts are species-appropriate.
